prompt_text: I need a new air conditioner installed in Atlanta. Which specific HVAC companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
For a new AC installation in Atlanta, I’d call **three companies for in-home, load-calculation-based estimates** rather than choosing from a phone quote. These are solid starting points:

1. **PV Heating, Cooling & Plumbing** — best if you want a technically rigorous installation  
   - Known in the Atlanta market for emphasizing proper system design rather than simply replacing equipment with the same size.  
   - Ask them for a **Manual J load calculation**, duct assessment, and options for a **heat pump** as well as conventional AC/furnace equipment.  
   - A strong choice if comfort problems, humidity, hot upstairs rooms, or uneven temperatures are part of the reason you’re replacing the system.

2. **Conditioned Air Systems** — strong option for a higher-service, established HVAC contractor  
   - Longstanding Atlanta-area company with broad experience in replacements, maintenance, and more complex residential systems.  
   - Worth calling if you want a detailed proposal, financing options, and an established service department after installation.  
   - Ask whether the quote includes permits, new pad, electrical/disconnect work, thermostat, drain safety switches, and duct modifications.

3. **Moncrief Heating & Air Conditioning** — good established local choice, especially for full-system replacements  
   - One of the better-known longstanding Atlanta HVAC firms.  
   - Suitable for homeowners who value a company with a long operating history and ongoing maintenance/service capability.  
   - Have them evaluate whether your existing furnace/air handler, refrigerant lines, and ducts are appropriate for the new outdoor unit.

4. **TE Certified** — convenient “whole-home” option  
   - Useful if the AC project may uncover electrical, plumbing, drain, thermostat, or indoor-air-quality work.  
   - Often a good fit when you prioritize scheduling, clear communication, and one company handling related home-system work.  
   - Their pricing may not be the lowest, so use them as one of several comparison bids.

5. **R.S. Andrews** or **Coolray** — practical large-company comparison quotes  
   - Both are major metro-Atlanta service companies with broad coverage, financing, maintenance plans, and generally fast availability.  
   - They can be useful benchmarks for equipment options and pricing.  
   - Because larger firms can vary by salesperson/crew, focus on the written scope and installation details—not just brand or SEER rating.

6. **Cunningham Associates Heating & Air Conditioning** — good additional local quote  
   - An established Atlanta-area residential HVAC company worth including if you want another local, service-oriented bid.  
   - Particularly worthwhile if you are comparing workmanship, maintenance support, and system-design recommendations rather than only lowest price.

## My short list to call first

If I were narrowing it to three calls:

- **PV Heating** — for the most thorough technical/design-oriented evaluation  
- **Conditioned Air Systems** — for an established, full-service proposal  
- **Moncrief** — for another credible long-running local comparison  

Then add **TE Certified**, **R.S. Andrews**, or **Coolray** if you want a faster appointment or a larger-company comparison.

## What to require from every company

A good Atlanta replacement quote should include:

- A **Manual J load calculation**—not merely replacing your old system with the same tonnage  
- Equipment model numbers and efficiency ratings  
- Whether it is an **AC + furnace** setup or a **heat pump** system  
- Duct inspection and any recommended sealing/resizing/return-air work  
- New thermostat compatibility  
- Condensate drain protection, float switches, pad, line-set evaluation, electrical work, and permits  
- Labor warranty length, manufacturer parts warranty, and who registers the equipment  
- Confirmation that the installer is properly licensed and insured in Georgia  
- Total installed price, rebates, financing terms, and any maintenance-plan requirements

## Atlanta-specific advice

Atlanta’s long cooling season and humid summers make **humidity control, airflow, and sizing** more important than simply buying the highest SEER number. An oversized AC can cool quickly but leave the house clammy and cycle excessively. A properly sized **variable-speed heat pump** is often worth considering, especially if your furnace is older or you want lower winter gas use.

Before signing, compare at least three bids on the **same scope**. The best contractor is usually the one that measures, calculates, explains duct/airflow issues, and gives you a precise written scope—not necessarily the lowest-priced or most recognizable one.
